ogTitle: Where to Stay in Lamai, Koh Samui
ogDesc: The best hotels in Lamai by budget.
intro: Lamai sits on Koh Samui's east coast, about 15 minutes south of Chaweng by car. People like it for a long beach and clear water close to Chaweng's quality, but with a more relaxed feel and rooms and meals that run roughly 20-30% cheaper. The beach splits loosely into a central stretch with shops, massage places, bars, and a night market, and quieter ends on either side. Just south is the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rock formation, a quick photo stop known for its oddly shaped boulders. The upscale resorts sit on the hillsides around the bay with full sea views. There's no convenient public transit here, so getting around the island usually means a taxi, a songthaew, or a rented scooter.

blocks.html: Short answer: Lamai is Koh Samui's second-biggest beach, quieter and better value than Chaweng. The sand runs about 4 km, the water is clear, and there are enough restaurants and bars to wander without the crowds of Chaweng. Stays range from beachfront bungalows starting around ฿900 to hillside pool villas with sea views in the five figures. A good fit for couples and families who want a solid beach on a lighter budget.

items.name: Bill Resort
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Budget · garden bungalows · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A long-running Lamai resort at the southern end of the beach, near the Samui Museum Village. The draw is Thai-style bungalows set in leafy gardens, with traditional decor and rooms that feel larger than the price. There's an outdoor pool with a children's section, and the sand is a few minutes' walk away. Rates start very low for a near-beach spot. Reviews praise the spacious rooms and the shady, relaxed grounds, though parts of the property are dated and could use upkeep. Good for budget travellers who aren't fussed about a polished finish.

items.name: Lamai Wanta Beach Resort
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Beachfront · central Lamai · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 3-star resort set right on Lamai Beach in the middle of the strip, where you can step from the pool onto the sand. It has an infinity-edge pool facing the sea and a mix of rooms and villas, including sea-view villas and family bungalows. Shops, banks, and restaurants are an easy walk away. The selling point is a central beachfront location that puts everything within reach, at a fair price for a beach property. A solid choice if you want a walkable base and a sea view to wake up to.

items.name: Aloha Resort Koh Samui
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Value · big beachfront pool · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A long-established Lamai beachfront resort known for value. It has a large pool with a kids' section and a jacuzzi, and the beach is a few minutes' walk from the grounds. The surrounding area is full of restaurants and massage shops, and there are two on-site restaurants plus a spa. Rooms are simply styled, with some on the older side but kept clean. Reviews highlight the beachfront location and the big pool; rooms are honestly not new. Best for families or couples who care more about location and the pool than a luxury finish.

items.name: Weekender Resort
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Families · beachfront pool villas · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A Lamai beachfront resort offering both rooms and pool villas, with the grounds opening straight onto the sand. There's an outdoor pool and a beachside restaurant and bar, and the Coco Splash waterpark is about a 9-minute walk away. Some villas have a private pool and are roomy enough for a family. Reviews single out the friendly staff and the beachfront setting. A good fit for families who want more space and the privacy of a villa at a reasonable 4-star price.

items.name: Renaissance Koh Samui Resort & Spa
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Luxury · sea-view pool villas · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 5-star Marriott resort at a quieter end of Lamai Bay, split across two sides of a road: rooms and suites on one, private sea-view pool villas on the other. It has a spa, several restaurants, and a private beach. The villas with their own pools draw the most praise from guests. Reviews highlight the service, sea views, and privacy, though some note the location is a bit removed from the main strip and needs a ride. Best for couples or families who want a quiet, upscale villa by the sea.

items.name: Silavadee Pool Spa Resort
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Luxury · clifftop pool villas · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A luxury resort built in tiers on a cliff above a small bay at the south end of Lamai, with 44 pool villas and around 36 deluxe rooms. Many villas have a private infinity pool facing the sea. The selling points are the panoramic bay views and the privacy. There are several restaurants, including a rooftop sea-view bar, plus a spa. Reviews praise the upscale feel and the attentive staff. Worth noting: the resort is on a steep hillside, so you rely on the internal shuttle to get up and down, and parts have seen renovation. Best for couples and honeymooners who want big views.

items.name: Banyan Tree Samui
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Top luxury · all-villa pool resort · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: The top luxury resort in Lamai, set on a private hill cove that cascades down to the bay. It has 88 villas, every one with a private infinity pool, and some types add an outdoor hot tub. Highlights include the large Banyan Tree Spa, five dining venues, and a private beach. It consistently ranks among the island's best for service and cleanliness. Reviews single out the privacy and the level of care. It's the priciest option in the area, best for honeymoons, special occasions, or anyone who wants a full private-villa experience.

faq.q: How is Lamai different from Chaweng, and who is it for?
faq.a: Lamai is Samui's second-biggest beach, with a long stretch of sand and clear water close to Chaweng's, but quieter, with less nightlife and rooms and meals roughly 20-30% cheaper. It suits couples, families, and anyone after a genuine rest. If you want a full strip of bars, clubs, late-night buzz, and lots of shopping, Chaweng fits better. Lamai still has a moderate cluster of bars and a night market along the central beach to wander.

faq.q: Is it easy to get around from Lamai, and do I need to rent a vehicle?
faq.a: There's no train or strong public transit here. Getting to Chaweng, Samui Airport, or the piers usually means a taxi, a songthaew, or a hotel car. If you plan several days of island sightseeing, renting a scooter is more flexible and cheaper, though some roads, especially the climbs up to hillside resorts, are steep and winding, so drive carefully if you're not used to them. Island taxis are fairly pricey and often don't use the meter, so agree on the fare before you get in.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Lamai, and what's the sea like?
faq.a: Samui is on the Gulf of Thailand, so its seasons differ from Phuket's. The driest, most reliable weather is roughly February to April, with clear water and calm seas. The heaviest rain falls from October to December, when you may get some swell and seaweed washing onto the beach. Lamai faces east; the water is fairly clear and shallow along the near shore, good for swimming. At low tide the sand widens and the water gets shallower, so check the tide times if you want deeper water.
